races.name: Yorkshire Dales Distillery/EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes(for Horses In Bands B, C And D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Neverbeatdeswalker
runners_data.note: Placed twice in two Good-ground runs and carries natural hold-up tendencies, though the field depth means Jack Garritty may be forced to place this runner far closer to the pace than Mark Walford typically deploys it; 42-day break adds a small fitness query.|

runners_data.name: Shaniko
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope is the standout jockey booking here, and Shaniko's four-run form showing consistent placed efforts on Good turf at 5f gives it solid claims — though its back-to-the-field instincts mean Tudhope will need to be proactive to get it into contention in a bunch finish.|

runners_data.name: Mugheer
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke debutant who is an unknown quantity on style and going, but Burke's two-year-old runners at sprint trips regularly show early pace and the stable's 8/43 form over 14 days suggests it is in a decent run of form; this horse could set the standard if it brings natural speed.|

runners_data.name: North Coates
runners_data.note: Shaped modestly on debut at 6f Good ground, finishing fifth, and drops to 5f now for Michael & David Easterby — Billy Garritty has ridden it before and knows its tendencies, but its true hold-up style is a potential handicap here and it has not shown enough raw ability yet to overcome a poor position.|

runners_data.name: Redrosecastana
runners_data.note: Finished ninth on debut at 6f Good and carries a fade-in-finish flag; Christopher Kellett's yard has shown limited 14-day form at 0/3 and this runner's profile suggests it needs things to fall perfectly, making it among the most unlikely to win from any scenario.|

runners_data.name: Romidijo
runners_data.note: The most experienced runner in the field with six career starts and two placed efforts at 5f on Good ground, giving it a meaningful form edge; Charlie Clover's yard is in fair recent form and Sam James is a capable pilot, though the horse's natural hold-up style means it needs gaps to appear in a compressed finish.|

runners_data.name: Scottys Rocket
runners_data.note: Sole start ended in a ninth-place finish at 5f Good with a fade noted, and Brian Ellison's yard is 2/26 over 14 days which is moderate; 37-day break combined with the finish-fade flag makes this one of the harder cases to construct a winning scenario around.|

runners_data.name: Ghazalia
runners_data.note: Debut runner for Hilal Kobeissi, a yard with minimal recent strike-rate at 0/1 over 14 days and an unknown style classification; Sean D Bowen is a competent jockey who could extract early pace if the horse shows it, making Ghazalia an unpredictable wildcard in terms of what position it occupies early.|

runners_data.name: Purrista
runners_data.note: Ran a fair third on Good ground at 5f on her second start for Gemma Tutty, and Connor Beasley keeps the ride with continuity of knowledge — her hold-up profile means she needs this race to set up as a genuine sprint finish, but she has shown enough placed form to merit respect if that shape materialises.|

races.paceDynamic: With no confirmed front-runner in a nine-runner 5f maiden, this race lacks a natural pace-setter and is likely to drift into a tactical sprint finish where early positioning becomes a lottery. The field is loaded with hold-up types — Neverbeatdeswalker, Shaniko, North Coates, Romidijo, Redrosecastana, Scottys Rocket and Purrista all prefer to race off the pace — meaning the early gallop will be modest at best unless the two unknown quantities Mugheer and Ghazalia show natural speed on debut. Whoever can quicken earliest out of a compressed midfield group will hold a significant advantage, as there is no dominant force to string the race out. This race shape favours horses with a sharp turn of foot who can act on Good turf and travel prominently without needing to be covered up, since genuine hold-up tactics will be undermined by the compressed nature of the contest. The field holds far more hold-up types than can realistically operate from the rear; of those redistributed to midfield, Shaniko (Daniel Tudhope) and Romidijo (multiple placed runs) are most likely to secure a workable position from which they can deliver their effort.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Debut Speedsters Dictate
scenarios.trigger: If Mugheer or Ghazalia show natural early pace on debut and set a modest but genuine gallop.
scenarios.body: With the held-up types struggling to position naturally, a debutant showing front-running speed would control the race from the front on a flat 5f track and simply stay there against limited opposition. This shape rewards horses with latent ability making a clean start, as the compressed hold-up horses behind would lack room and time to close.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Sprint-Finish Blanket
scenarios.trigger: If no horse settles into a lead and the field crawls, producing a sprint from the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: Every runner converges in a tight group, turning this into a raw speed test over the final two furlongs on Good turf where the horse with the sharpest acceleration wins regardless of tactical position. Shaniko (Daniel Tudhope) and Romidijo, who both carry placed form and have shown the ability to quicken in sprint finishes, are best placed to capitalise from this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Lone Pacer Snatches It
scenarios.trigger: If one of the redistributed hold-up horses breaks smartly and grabs a solo lead by accident before rivals can react.
scenarios.body: A lone runner setting a dawdling pace unchallenged on Good ground over 5f at Catterick can steal several lengths on rivals who are all waiting on each other, and the race is over before it begins. North Coates and Neverbeatdeswalker, both lightly raced and unknown quantities at this level, could benefit if their jockeys make an aggressive early decision.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Caught Wide
scenarios.trigger: If pace is set but the held-up horses get caught in traffic and fail to find a clean run through the closing stages.
scenarios.body: True hold-up tactics backfire in a field this size over a flat 5f when a genuine pace is set, as late challengers must navigate a wall of horses with insufficient rail to travel down. Redrosecastana and Scottys Rocket, both of whom faded in their sole starts, represent the lowest probability of delivering from this shape and are the most exposed horses if the race unfolds this way.

watchPoints.text: Tudhope on Shaniko — if he positions this horse closer than its natural style demands in the opening furlong, it becomes a leading player in any scenario involving a sprint finish over this flat 5f trip.
Mugheer and Ghazalia are both debutants with unknown pace profiles; if either breaks sharply and shows natural speed, the entire race shape will be reset around them in the opening two furlongs.

The fade-in-finish flags on both Redrosecastana and Scottys Rocket mean any scenario producing a strong early pace is particularly damaging to their prospects — watch the market to see if punters have discounted them accordingly.

With seven of nine runners carrying genuine hold-up tendencies, the opening furlong of this 5f may be unusually slow — watch for a scramble at halfway as jockeys realise no one has gone forward and suddenly the race becomes a 2.5f sprint from standstill.

races.name: Berber Leather Maiden Stakes (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: Aurora's Doublesix
runners_data.note: Brian Rothwell's 4-year-old has posted a consistent string of poor finishes (0W0P in 15 similar-going runs) and is a genuine hold-up performer who will find herself further forward than natural given the number of hold-up types in this field — the style mismatch tempers her already modest prospects considerably.

runners_data.name: Khanimambo
runners_data.note: David Nolan partners this Barron-trained 3-year-old who has just one run to her name — a seventh at 7f on good ground — making her deeply unexposed but also with no evidence of improvement; the trip and going are familiar, but form data is near-absent.

runners_data.name: Skewsby
runners_data.note: Michael and David Easterby's runner is flagged with completely unknown going preference and is lightly raced, making her the biggest unknown quantity in the field; Billy Garritty rides and any market support on the day should be noted given the absence of form signals.

runners_data.name: Dreamadera
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's 3-year-old returns after 123 days off the track, a substantial absence that is the primary concern; her two runs show a seventh and a twelfth, both in ordinary maiden company, and the hold-up style sits awkwardly in a race that will be genuinely contested up front.

runners_data.name: Lady Gormire
runners_data.note: Connor Beasley partners this Michael Dods-trained front-runner who brings solid placed form (3P from 6 runs on similar going) including a second at 7f on good, making her the most battle-tested pace-setter in the field; she will fight for the lead with Royale Union and her stamina at the trip is proven.

runners_data.name: Moonlight Melody
runners_data.note: Donald McCain's 3-year-old ran three consecutive fourths and has placed form at 7f on good ground, which reads well on paper — but as a true hold-up horse pushed into midfield by the redistribution, she is unlikely to race in her optimal position, which meaningfully reduces her chance of delivering a winning run.

runners_data.name: Royale Union
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's yard is in sharp 14-day form (8/43) and Clifford Lee takes the ride on this confirmed front-runner who has placed at both 6f and 7f on good going; she will press for the lead immediately and her placed record suggests she competes hard even under pressure, though being fully extended early is the obvious risk.

runners_data.name: Soca Star
runners_data.note: Seb Spencer's 3-year-old carries consistent prominent-style form, placing seven times from twelve runs on similar going, and arrives fresh on just 8 days' turnaround; Dale Swift rides and the horse's ability to sit just off a genuine pace and finish off a competitive gallop makes this a structurally well-suited runner for the expected race shape.

races.paceDynamic: Royale Union and Lady Gormire are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the off over Catterick's 7f on good ground, creating an honest, genuine gallop that is unlikely to slacken at any stage. With two genuine pace-setters pulling against each other, the tempo should be sustained rather than stop-start, which historically at Catterick favours horses travelling smoothly in behind rather than those expending energy fighting for position early. Soca Star should slot in just behind the duelling leaders as the most naturally prominent type, while the redistribution note is critical: Moonlight Melody and Aurora's Doublesix are genuine hold-up performers who have been mapped to midfield because the field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Lady Gormire and Royale Union are best placed to secure their natural positions, leaving the redistributed pair racing further forward than ideal. The tactical verdict is clear: a contested pace over 7f on good ground at Catterick should set things up for a prominent or stalking mid-division runner to pick up the pieces late, with those racing prominently in a genuine rhythm behind the leaders holding the structural advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Stalker Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Royale Union and Lady Gormire fight for supremacy and set a genuine honest gallop that softens both front-runners in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A horse sitting smoothly in second or third gear behind the duel conserves energy and pounces as the pace-setters tie up; Soca Star, having shown consistent prominence and placed form on good ground, is ideally positioned for this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dictates Clean
scenarios.trigger: If one of the front-runners — most likely Royale Union — gains a small early advantage and Lady Gormire is restrained or outpaced, allowing a lone leader to control tempo.
scenarios.body: Royale Union, trained by K.R. Burke who is in strong 14-day form (8/43), has placed form at 7f on good ground and could get an uncontested lead if Lady Gormire fails to match early strides; controlling the pace from the front at Catterick over 7f with no pressure is a significant advantage.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Run Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the contested early pace is fierce enough to burn out the front-runners dramatically, creating a late-closing opportunity deeper into the field.
scenarios.body: Moonlight Melody has placed form at 7f on good ground and Donald McCain's runner would benefit from a genuine end-to-end gallop if able to find a clear run; however, both Moonlight Melody and Aurora's Doublesix are racing out of their natural hold-up role, making this scenario structurally less likely.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Implodes, Maiden Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners tie each other up so completely that the race is thrown open to lightly-raced or unexposed types finishing off a slowly-run final quarter.
scenarios.body: Skewsby is entirely unknown (UNKNOWN going, lightly raced flag, no form string available) and could be a dark horse if the race falls apart; Khanimambo, a Barron-trained type with one run at this trip and going, is similarly unexposed and could benefit from an unusual scenario.

watchPoints.text: Royale Union and Lady Gormire will go head-to-head for the lead from the first stride — watch whether either jockey concedes position early, as a solo leader changes the entire shape of the race.

Moonlight Melody and Aurora's Doublesix are both natural hold-up horses who will be pushed further forward than ideal by the race dynamic — if either appears to be held up at the back regardless, they may be sacrificing ground they cannot recover over 7f.

Skewsby is a complete unknown: watch the market closely pre-race, as significant support for this Michael and David Easterby runner could signal stable confidence that the form data simply cannot reveal.

Soca Star returns just 8 days after its last run — watch the paddock and early market move to confirm the horse is travelling well, as quick turnarounds for Seb Spencer's yard carry a modest strike rate (0/12 in 14-day window).

Dreamadera's 123-day layoff for the Tim Easterby yard is notable; Easterby has a strong overall strike rate (3/94 in 14 days is volume-based) but a horse returning from four months off into a maiden on good ground deserves caution unless showing well in pre-race market signals.

races.name: Happy 50th Birthday Victoria Melling Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Run This Way
runners_data.note: Paul Midgley's eight-year-old has two recent wins over 6f on Good ground and is the chief stalker to Overbudget; David Nolan rides with purpose from a prominent position and the Good surface is confirmed fine for this mare, though 81 days off the track is worth monitoring.|

runners_data.name: Miss Willows
runners_data.note: Simon Whitaker's seven-year-old returned from 12 days ago and won over 7f on Soft, but her last two runs over 6f on Good produced a 10th and 11th — the shorter, faster trip on this surface is a clear concern for a hold-up horse needing a strong pace that may not materialise.|

runners_data.name: Barmyblade
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby has three winners in 14 days and this four-year-old showed ability when winning over 6f on Good (1/6f/GOO twice in last five), with the tongue-tie noted; returning on nine days' rest looks fine, and David Allan's experience at northern venues is an asset, making this one a credible each-way threat if pace forces its hand.|

runners_data.name: Overbudget
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's three-year-old is the race-shaper here, likely to lead and control from the off, but the STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) and form figures of 283769 suggest it is vulnerable once collared — the question is simply whether anything gets close enough to challenge on what looks a sustainable tempo.|

runners_data.name: Powernap
runners_data.note: Jessica Bedi's three-year-old has placed form on Good ground and showed ability when winning on Soft, but as a genuine hold-up type pushed into a midfield mapping by the congested rear, its natural finishing run is compromised; the 48-day absence and STYLE_FIT flag together mean this is harder to win from than the map position implies.|

runners_data.name: Battenburg Belle
runners_data.note: Rebecca Menzies's three-year-old has consistent placing form including a recent 3/6f/GOO, and won over 6f on Good earlier in her last five — genuinely effective at this trip on this surface, but racing in a cluster of similar hold-up types means she is unlikely to find the clear gap she needs from her natural style, and the STYLE_FIT flag tempers her claims accordingly.|

races.paceDynamic: Overbudget is the lone confirmed front-runner in a six-runner field and, with no rival likely to push hard for the lead, should be able to control tempo from the outset at Catterick's straight six furlongs on Good ground. Run This Way is the one prominent-style horse who could press for position early, but the pace she exerts is unlikely to be aggressive enough to unsettle Overbudget's rhythm. The field holds more hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Powernap and Battenburg Belle are genuine come-from-behind types who will struggle to find their natural position with so many rivals sharing similar instincts, meaning both are likely to race closer to midfield than ideal. A sustainable, controlled pace set by one uncontested leader on Good turf at a flat, straight track historically favours horses racing prominently or just off the front, as the sectionals rarely compress enough for true closers to reel in a fresh-legged front-runner.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Overbudget Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Overbudget is allowed to stride clear from the stalls and control tempo without sustained pressure from Run This Way.
scenarios.body: Overbudget sets a comfortable, metronomic gallop down Catterick's straight six and, with no rival burning energy to close the gap, has enough in reserve to repel challengers in the final furlong; the Good ground and flat configuration suit a horse able to dictate its own rhythm.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Runs Down Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Run This Way tracks Overbudget closely throughout and the combination of early pace and a sustained challenge proves enough to wear the leader down.
scenarios.body: Run This Way has winning form over exactly this trip and going combination (1/6f/GOO twice in recent history) and, sitting a length or two off the leader, could accelerate past a tiring Overbudget inside the final furlong; Paul Midgley's runner has shown this form is genuine and David Nolan's positive riding style suits this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Finish Fast Late
scenarios.trigger: If Overbudget sets a stronger gallop than anticipated and the pace genuinely compromises front-end stamina, leaving a window for the hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: Barmyblade has strong Good-ground form at 6f and, with Tim Easterby's stable in good order (T14: 3/94), could pick off tiring rivals in the closing stages; Battenburg Belle has placed form at this trip on similar going but the redistribution away from her natural hold-up position reduces her chance of producing her best.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Sprints Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or a significant incident disrupts the front two, opening a gap for a fresh-legged runner coming from off the pace.
scenarios.body: Miss Willows or Powernap, both running from further back than ideal given the crowded hold-up group, could benefit from a chaotic finish if things go wrong for the leaders; however, both carry the handicap of racing out of their natural role and neither's recent form over this course and distance inspires confidence in this scenario.

watchPoints.text: Overbudget's front-running position is pivotal — if Andrew Mullen is caught flat-footed from the stalls and Run This Way steals the lead instead, the entire race shape inverts and prominent-style runners gain a significant advantage.

The congestion of hold-up types (Powernap, Battenburg Belle, Miss Willows, Barmyblade) means the back half of the field could be bunched entering the straight — watch for traffic issues or interference that could cost genuine closers a clear run.

Run This Way's 81-day absence is the key unknown for the most likely prominent-tracking scenario; if there is any fitness hangover, Overbudget may simply sustain its lead all the way to the line unchallenged.

Barmyblade's tongue-tie and Tim Easterby's in-form stable (3 from 94 in 14 days is modest but active) warrant monitoring in the betting — if the hold-up group gets a clean run, this four-year-old's Good-ground 6f wins make it the most credible late challenger.

races.name: Hats Of Yorkshire Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Animato
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up performer for Donald McCain with consistent form at 1m6f-2m1f on Good ground, including two top-three finishes at this sort of trip; David Nolan takes the ride and the horse is likely to be delivered late, meaning a clear passage is essential given the congested midfield in this field.

runners_data.name: Zephlyn
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the race and therefore a pivotal tactical force; Ewan Whillans's seven-year-old has six runs over 1m6f at Good Catterick-style tracks with two wins and three placed efforts in similar conditions, and an uncontested lead over this flat mile and three-quarters suits its profile ideally.

runners_data.name: Mr Withington
runners_data.note: Connor Beasley partners this five-year-old Whillans runner, a natural hold-up horse whose best trip form at 1m-1m4f on Good ground is marginally short of today's 1m6f; shown in midfield on the map because the rear is oversubscribed, though his true inclination is to race from behind and he may need a pace collapse to get competitive.

runners_data.name: Niffler
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's three-year-old arrives on a six-day turnaround with a remarkable recent form reversal — winning over 1m4f at Sandown after two distant efforts — but the fading-in-finish flag is a concern at 1m6f; Luke Morris partners and the horse's true style is rearward, placed in midfield here only by necessity, with the trip extension the key unknown.

runners_data.name: Fairydale
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's three-year-old filly has two placed efforts from eight starts at 1m4f-1m6f on Good ground and David Allan rides; a hold-up performer by inclination who is shown in midfield only because the rear is crowded, and her best chance rests on tracking closer than usual and catching a pace that flattens Zephlyn.

runners_data.name: This Rib
runners_data.note: Joanna Mason rides this David Loughnane three-year-old, which has modest turf form at 1m-1m4f on Good going and a pulled-up effort in recent starts casting a shadow over current soundness; the horse's natural position is from behind, but with the rear blocked it must race against type in midfield, and its turf record suggests it is vulnerable at this level.

runners_data.name: Manbearpig
runners_data.note: Rebecca Menzies's three-year-old has placed twice from seven starts at 1m2f-1m6f but trainer has zero wins from ten runners in the past fortnight; Faleh Bughanaim rides and the horse gravitates to a rearward position naturally, so being pushed into midfield by the crowded hold-up contingent means it faces an unfamiliar positional challenge.

runners_data.name: Lilykoy
runners_data.note: Dylan Cunha's three-year-old showed fair form when third at 2m on Good ground most recently, suggesting the step up to 1m6f is no issue on this evidence; Alex Jary claims three pounds on a horse whose instinct is to race from the back, and while shown in midfield on the map, a clear run from the rear would be needed for the stable's 35-day absentee to make an impact.

races.paceDynamic: Zephlyn is the sole identified front-runner in this 1m6f Catterick handicap and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, is set to bowl along at a sustainable, uncontested gallop that will keep the pace honest without being truly searching over this trip. The absence of pressure on the leader creates a steadily-run scenario where the race is likely to be won from the front or close to it, as those in rear will face a wall of horses when the tempo lifts approaching the home turn. Critically, this field is saturated with hold-up types — This Rib, Fairydale, Manbearpig, Niffler, Mr Withington and Lilykoy are all natural hold-up horses compressed into midfield positions on the map because there is nowhere further back for them all to go, meaning the closing runs of several will be compromised by traffic and positional disadvantage. The race shape strongly favours Zephlyn and any runner capable of travelling close to the pace, as a controlled gallop over 1m6f at Catterick rewards those who secure a forward position early and avoid the inevitable bunching further back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Zephlyn Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Zephlyn settles into an uncontested lead and controls a measured gallop throughout, denying those behind the strong early pace they need.
scenarios.body: Zephlyn bowls along comfortably at the head of affairs, the field strung out behind in a procession, and the modest tempo means fitness reserves are intact for a sustained run from the home turn; a hold-up field unable to generate momentum from rear cannot launch the kind of sweeping late move needed to collar an untroubled front-runner.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Midfield Traveller Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely steady enough that a prominent-tracking runner conserves energy and produces a decisive move turning for home.
scenarios.body: A horse like Fairydale or Lilykoy, both with placed form over this type of trip on Good ground, travels economically within the pack and hits the front at the right moment as Zephlyn's effort flattens out; this scenario depends on one of the redistributed hold-up types getting a clean run through, which the crowded midfield makes uncertain.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Gets Through
scenarios.trigger: If the field bunches and a gap opens late, allowing a genuine hold-up horse to thread through from rear to collar tiring leaders in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Niffler, stepping markedly up in trip from recent Sandown form and trained by the high-strike-rate Sir Mark Prescott, finds daylight after being held up off the steady pace and picks off the weakening leaders; the risk is the field never opens up enough over this flat track for a wide late run to materialise in time.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Falls Back
scenarios.trigger: If Zephlyn over-reaches on the front end without the benefit of genuine company and ties up in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: With Zephlyn unable to sustain its lead, the race becomes a sprint for the line among those who tracked closest and conserved most energy; Animato, with solid placed form at 1m6f-2m1f on Good going, is best placed to pick up the pieces having raced from a patient hold-up position.

watchPoints.text: Zephlyn sets a suspiciously slow early gallop — if the opening half-mile fractions are unusually leisurely, the entire hold-up division behind will fail to get competitive and the race becomes a tactical sprint that plays entirely into Zephlyn's hands.

The midfield is packed with six horses of broadly similar ability and natural hold-up style; watch for traffic problems approaching the home turn at Catterick, where the course narrows and a bunched field can leave several runners with nowhere to go at a critical moment.

Niffler's fading-in-finish flag combined with the step up to 1m6f is a live concern — watch whether Luke Morris commits early or is forced wide, as a horse that has already shown it stops in the final furlong faces extra risk over a trip it has never attempted.

Ewan Whillans has two runners in the race (Zephlyn and Mr Withington) — watch how both are ridden from the start, as stable tactics could influence whether Zephlyn is asked to go faster than the race demands or Mr Withington is deliberately positioned to track its stablemate.

Tim Easterby's trainer-14-day strike rate of 3/94 is extremely low; note whether Fairydale jumps cleanly and travels fluently, as a yard out of form could mean the filly fails to produce the effort her placed form on paper might suggest.

races.name: Oops A Daisy Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Fidelius
runners_data.note: Consistent five-furlong performer with two seconds on Good going in recent outings; Alex Jary (3) claims 3lb and races from a prominent position where the congestion risk is real — the 18-day break looks straightforward for Nigel Tinkler, whose 14-day strike rate is modest at 1/20.|

runners_data.name: Marching Mac
runners_data.note: Won on Good ground at five furlongs last time out and Grace McEntee has a strong relationship with the Phil McEntee stable; the 75-day absence is the main query, but the tongue-tie is retained and Good going suits — a genuine hold-up horse who needs the pace to work in his favour.|

runners_data.name: Canon's House
runners_data.note: Michael and David Easterby send this one out just five days after its last run, which warrants monitoring for freshness; Billy Garritty partners a prominent racer with course and distance experience, though the recent form string of 506347 suggests it is in a difficult patch.|

runners_data.name: Novamay
runners_data.note: All five of the most recent runs in the historical sample came at six furlongs on Good or Good-to-Soft, so the drop to five furlongs on Good is a genuine query despite the strong place record — Rhys Elliott's 5lb claim helps offset the rise in pace demands and Michael Dods's yard is in decent 14-day form at 3/22.|

runners_data.name: Secret Mistral
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the field and thus guaranteed a clean lead; Myla Coppins (5) aboard for Tony Carroll, who is striking at 3/30 over 14 days, and the record of 2W7P on similar going underlines she knows how to run on Good — the critical factor is whether a comfortable gallop hands her the race or invites challengers.|

runners_data.name: Angel Numbers
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins on Good ground at five furlongs make this three-year-old's recent form highly relevant; Jake Dickson (5) pilots for Ruth Carr, who is 2/24 over the last fortnight, and the hold-up style is perfectly suited to a race where the prominent group may tie each other up.|

runners_data.name: Call Margot
runners_data.note: Gemma Tutty's three-year-old has two wins and place form on Good ground but very modest recent finishes of 172600; though shown in midfield on the pace map, Call Margot is a genuine hold-up horse by nature — the race shape makes it unlikely she will find the position her form requires, tempering expectations.|

runners_data.name: Vince L'Amour
runners_data.note: Two wins on Good ground and experienced handler Tim Easterby in fine overall form at 3/94; however, by natural inclination a true hold-up horse, and the pace map has him mapped to midfield because the rear of the field is already crowded — racing slightly out of his comfort zone here, which is a material concern.|

runners_data.name: Our Absent Friends
runners_data.note: Jason Hart takes the ride for Tristan Davidson, who is an active 3/8 over 14 days — solid trainer momentum; Our Absent Friends has two wins at five furlongs on Good and races prominently, meaning he is right in the thick of the congestion battle and will need a clean passage at the two-furlong pole.|

runners_data.name: Canaria Queen
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby double-declares alongside Vince L'Amour; Duran Fentiman partners a prominent-style filly with strong place form on Good ground at five furlongs, headgear noted (p), and the 9-day turnaround for a yard in form suggests straightforward preparation — her risk is getting caught in the prominent scrimmage.|

races.paceDynamic: Secret Mistral is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival disputing the lead, she should cruise into a comfortable solo position from the gates and set a honest but not suicidal gallop on Good ground over five furlongs at Catterick. Behind her, Fidelius, Canon's House, Our Absent Friends and Canaria Queen all want to race prominently, creating a congested battle for the two or three places just off the pace between the two- and three-furlong markers — that scrimmaging is where traffic problems will materialise. Angel Numbers, Marching Mac and Novamay are the genuine hold-up types who will be patiently ridden from the rear, needing the pace to soften those ahead of them. The field holds more hold-up horses than the map can physically place at the rear: Call Margot and Vince L'Amour are true hold-up types redistributed to midfield because the real back-of-the-field slots are already taken by Angel Numbers, Marching Mac and Novamay — of those redistributed horses, neither is likely to get the true off-the-pace position their form demands. This shape — a lone, uncontested leader setting a controlled pace with a cluttered prominent group behind — strongly favours hold-up horses with a genuine late kick, particularly those with proven form on Good ground at five furlongs who can sidestep the prominent-group scrimmage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Secret Mistral Controls, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Secret Mistral leads unchallenged and sets a fair but comfortable gallop, allowing hold-up horses to pick up and mow her down late.
scenarios.body: Secret Mistral dictates from the front at a measured tempo, but the clustering of four prominent types just behind her creates interference and burning energy around the two-furlong pole, leaving the patient hold-up horses with clear daylight to finish through. Angel Numbers and Marching Mac, both proven winners on Good ground at five furlongs, are ideally placed to sweep past a tiring pack inside the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Congestion Causes Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the four prominent-style horses scrimmage hard for position in the first two furlongs and the pace heats up significantly.
scenarios.body: The battle between Fidelius, Canon's House, Our Absent Friends and Canaria Queen behind Secret Mistral turns the race into a genuine test, stretching the field and injecting enough pace to reward a runner who gets a clean, unimpeded passage from midfield. Fidelius, who has finished second twice on Good and has consistent five-furlong form, and Canaria Queen, who has strong place form on Good going, are most likely to emerge from the scrimmage with enough left to land a blow.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Secret Mistral Outstays the Field
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow enough that Secret Mistral's lead is never seriously threatened and she simply kicks clear off a false gallop.
scenarios.body: A truly modest early tempo allows Secret Mistral to dictate every yard without burning energy, and the closers find themselves stuck behind the prominent scrimmage with no momentum to close the gap in time. Secret Mistral's strong record on Good ground at five furlongs — three placings and two wins in similar conditions — underlines she is entirely capable of making all on a day when no one presses her.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Types Defy the Map
scenarios.trigger: If Call Margot or Vince L'Amour manage to get further back than their mapped position and produce a genuine late run.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires the prominent group ahead to produce enough pace to open a gap for these two horses to exploit, which is possible but materially less likely given neither is guaranteed to find their natural hold-up position in this race shape. Vince L'Amour's two wins on Good ground offer some appeal if the stars align, but the [STYLE_FIT] discount on both horses makes this a low-probability outcome that should not be backed confidently without seeing early race positioning first.

watchPoints.text: Secret Mistral leads unchallenged from the gates — if Myla Coppins is allowed to dictate an uncontested pace, monitor whether the four prominent horses (Fidelius, Canon's House, Our Absent Friends, Canaria Queen) burn energy scrimmaging behind her, as that congestion is the key pace pivot for the whole race.

Angel Numbers is the hold-up horse with the most relevant recent form (back-to-back wins on Good at 5f) — watch her position at the two-furlong pole, as any traffic from the prominent scrimmage ahead could cost her the race even if she is travelling best.

Marching Mac returns after 75 days off — if Grace McEntee settles her smoothly in the early stages and she begins to travel well approaching halfway, the fitness query may be irrelevant and she becomes a serious threat from the rear.

Call Margot and Vince L'Amour are both true hold-up horses mapped to midfield; if either gets shuffled further back than their map position suggests, they could find genuine late running room — but watch their actual gate-to-two-furlong positioning before drawing conclusions.

Novamay has run exclusively at six furlongs in all five recent starts — the step down to five furlongs on Good is untested in this form cycle; if she travels strongly in the first half of the race, the trip question is answered early, but a fading display would confirm the five-furlong trip is a concern.

races.name: Celebrate National Racehorse Week Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Bizarre Law
runners_data.note: A seven-year-old hold-up type returning after 49 days off, with a recent win over 7f on Soft and placing form on Good; the lengthy absence is a notable concern and, with the field stacked with hold-up horses, is unlikely to get anywhere near its natural rearmost position in running.

runners_data.name: Golden Prosperity
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed pace-setter from Tony Coyle & Kaine Wood's yard, returning 19 days after its last run with strong Good-going form (12/15 sim-going strikes including 1W5P); Jake Dickson's 5lb claim is a useful weight allowance and this horse's ability to control fractions unchallenged is the defining tactical fact of this race.

runners_data.name: I Can Boogy
runners_data.note: A four-year-old hold-up performer for Nigel Tinkler with a placed record over 7f-8f, better suited to further than this 7f trip and likely to find itself shuffled back in the pack; the trainer's 1/20 14-day strike rate provides little confidence, and its sim-going record shows no wins from eight starts.

runners_data.name: Mister Sky Blue
runners_data.note: A prominent-tracking four-year-old who is equipped to sit just behind Golden Prosperity and represents the most natural second-position runner in the field; Gemma Tutty's runner has decent Good-going placing form (0W3P from 8 runs) and 14 days since its last run suggests it should be cherry-ripe.

runners_data.name: Moral Victory
runners_data.note: Very limited recent form — finishing 8th and 12th in recent starts — and the fades-in-finish flag is damning in a race where hold-up horses already face structural disadvantage; Lawrence Mullaney has a modest 1/6 14-day record and this horse's Going history of only 1 sim-going run from 3 is paper-thin.

runners_data.name: Rain Cap
runners_data.note: A nine-year-old veteran with a genuine Good-going record (1W5P from 9 sim-going runs) and visor headgear retained; one of the few hold-up horses with a credible closing profile for this trip, though 22 days off and a trainer with a 0/2 14-day record dampen the angle slightly.

runners_data.name: Ridgemaster
runners_data.note: A four-year-old hold-up type for Simon Waugh who has placed twice on Soft/Good over 6f-7f; the trainer has zero runners in the 14-day window giving no recent data, and the horse's best form has come on Soft rather than the Good ground in place today.

runners_data.name: Without Delay
runners_data.note: Connor Beasley takes the ride on this seven-year-old hold-up type who has strong Good-going placing form (0W3P from 12 sim-going runs) and wears a visor; best effort was a 2nd over 7f Good which precisely mirrors today's conditions, though the step back from a recent 9th over further suggests the shorter trip is welcome.

runners_data.name: Belling The Cat
runners_data.note: A three-year-old from Tony Coyle & Kaine Wood who holds natural hold-up tendencies but will struggle to find that position in a rear-heavy field; the 3lb apprentice allowance for David Nolan is not enough to compensate for a form string showing three consecutive placed efforts that have now drifted to a 7th and 8th.

runners_data.name: Dee's Honey
runners_data.note: Jason Hart takes the ride on this three-year-old who carries a fades-in-finish flag — a significant concern for a horse already likely to be racing out of its preferred rear position; only 12 days since its last run, but a form string of four 9s and 5s on Good gives no basis for confidence.

runners_data.name: Lanarra
runners_data.note: James Sullivan partners this lightly-raced three-year-old for R Mike Smith who has placed twice on Good over 6f and shows consistent form (-23435); a natural hold-up horse who holds some claims if Sullivan can manoeuvre into a prominent position, though being unable to secure that role in this field makes the task harder.

runners_data.name: Runninman
runners_data.note: A three-year-old wearing a tongue-tie and padding headgear for Donald Whillans, freshest in the field at just 7 days since its last run; its sim-going record produces no wins from 4 runs and its hist shows a pattern of mid-to-rear finishes on Soft and Standard tracks — Good ground at Catterick is an unknown quantity.

runners_data.name: Ryefield
runners_data.note: Lawrence Mullaney's three-year-old carries a fades-in-finish warning and has a form string of 5-8807, the trajectory heading in entirely the wrong direction; five recent runs on Good or Standard all produced mid-to-rear finishes and there is no compelling reason to believe conditions suit today.

runners_data.name: Twilight Dawn
runners_data.note: A three-year-old who wears a hood for Simon Whitaker and has placed twice over 7f on Good ground — giving it the strongest case among the redistributed hold-up types if it can find competitive form; 32 days off since its last run and a natural hold-up style that will be squeezed by the field's composition, but its Goodground 7f placing record (0W2P) is at least relevant.

races.paceDynamic: Golden Prosperity is the one confirmed front-runner in this 14-runner field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should stride to the front unchallenged and control the tempo from the outset at Catterick's 7f. On Good ground with a modest pace likely to be set at a sustainable clip, the race will be run at a measured gallop through the first half before the field strings out on the turn and the sprint begins in earnest inside the final two furlongs. The vast majority of this field are natural hold-up types — Rain Cap, Without Delay, Ridgemaster, and Ryefield among those who will race from the rear — meaning the closing stages will see a wall of horses trying to make late ground against a horse who has had the race run entirely to its own tempo. Several runners tagged as redistributed — Lanarra, Bizarre Law, Twilight Dawn, Dee's Honey, Belling The Cat, Runninman, I Can Boogy, and Moral Victory — are genuine hold-up or prominent types who have been shifted forward on the map because the field is too hold-up heavy to reflect their true styles; Mister Sky Blue and Golden Prosperity are most likely to actually secure prominent positions. The tactical verdict is clear: a front-runner controlling its own pace on Good ground with no pressure strongly favours horses who can race prominently or stalk the leader through the race, as hold-up horses face the classic Catterick trap of being held up behind a muddling pace that never truly sets them up for a sustained finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Golden Prosperity Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Golden Prosperity sets a comfortable, uncontested gallop and the hold-up pack fails to close the gap in time.
scenarios.body: Golden Prosperity strides to the front without a challenger, dictates a fair but not overly generous pace, and has enough in reserve to hold on as the closers arrive too late on Catterick's undulating 7f track; on Good ground the front-runner's fitness from a recent run 19 days ago is a positive. Mister Sky Blue, tracking close throughout under Conor Whiteley, is best placed to challenge, while Rain Cap — one of the few genuine hold-up types with a win on Good going — has the best closing profile of the rear runners.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just fast enough to weaken Golden Prosperity in the final furlong, allowing the closest tracker to sweep past.
scenarios.body: A runner positioned just behind the leader — most likely Mister Sky Blue — uses the cover of Golden Prosperity's pace to travel sweetly before producing a decisive challenge inside the final furlong; Catterick's downhill finish rewards horses who can maintain momentum without needing a dramatic turn of foot. Lanarra, despite being a natural hold-up type displaced forward on the map, could also benefit here if James Sullivan pushes forward early and slots in behind the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Swamp The Field
scenarios.trigger: If Golden Prosperity sets a genuinely strong gallop that burns itself out, opening the door for closers to sweep through.
scenarios.body: A faster-than-expected pace from Golden Prosperity — perhaps pressured early by a prominent-tracking rival — would compress the final two furlongs into a flat-out sprint, giving true hold-up horses the legitimate run they need; Rain Cap has the going record (1W5P on Good/sim) and Without Delay has the most course-appropriate form profile for this scenario. However, this shape depends heavily on horses racing out of their redistributed roles performing as true closers, which tempers confidence significantly given the structural pace dynamics.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Midfield Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is so slow that midfield and hold-up horses get no cover and the race becomes a tactical dash from the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: A dawdling pace would bunch the entire field together turning in, effectively turning the race into a 2f sprint where positional advantage from mid-race counts for little; Twilight Dawn, who has placed three times over 7f on Good, and Ridgemaster, placed on Good ground over this trip, have the pace figures to fire out of a messy finish. This is the least likely shape given Golden Prosperity's confirmed front-running role and the expectation it will at least set a fair clip.

watchPoints.text: Golden Prosperity (Jake Dickson, 5lb claim) holds the critical tactical advantage as the unchallenged pace-setter — watch whether any rival, particularly Mister Sky Blue, attempts to press it early, as any such challenge would fundamentally alter the race shape.

The sheer volume of hold-up horses in this field — at least 10 of 14 runners — means significant traffic and positional congestion is likely in the straight; watch for Without Delay and Rain Cap, two of the more experienced closers, to be caught flat-footed if the field fans wide.

Ryefield and Moral Victory both carry fades-in-finish flags and are trained by the same handler (Lawrence Mullaney, 1/6 14-day); if either is prominent early, they are likely to empty and cause interference to closers making their run.

Dee's Honey — only 12 days since its last run and carrying the fades-in-finish tag — is worth monitoring in the paddock for signs of freshness or trainer intent, given Jason Hart's booking is a booking of note despite the horse's modest record on Good ground.

Runninman's headgear combination (tongue-tie plus tp) and its 7-day turnaround for Donald Whillans is worth noting — watch whether the stable expects it to race more forward than its hold-up style suggests, which could inject an element of pace pressure on Golden Prosperity unexpectedly.
